title: Desk connector v0
description: One contract for every connector, with three bindings: a Wasm component, an MCP server (ADR 0032) or a declarative HTTP binding the core runs (ADR 0106). A connector brings an app's data in as items and its actions as commands; it has no screen of its own.

ConnectorManifest.description: What a kind connector plugin declares under connector in plugin.json.

resources.description: The kinds of item the connector brings in, one entry per kind.

instanceSettings.description: What the person fills in for each instance, by name (a folder, an account, a token).

ConnectorBinding.description: How the connector runs: wasm, a component the plugin's entry names (no VM to boot); mcp, an MCP server inside the VM that follows the Desk profile in the README; http, requests and a mapping the core runs from the http block, with no code of the plugin's own (ADR 0106).

ConnectorAuthKind.description: none (local files, the OS's own data), token (a key the person pastes) or oauth.

ConnectorAuth.description: How an instance signs in. Tokens are kept by the core and never handed to the connector's code; with binding http the core itself sends the token (http.auth). No v0 method starts an OAuth flow yet.

title.description: What the person is asked for: Personal access token.

HttpBinding.description: A connector as data (binding http): GET requests against one base URL, each response's pages followed, and every record mapped into an item. The core runs it, reads the token from the instance's secret setting and sends it only to the base URL's origin; the token never crosses the bridge. Each sync reads every page again and removes the items that left (ADR 0106).

headers.description: Sent with every request: Accept, an API version. Never Authorization (auth says how the token goes) and never a secret.

requests.description: What one sync asks for, in order. The same item from two requests is one item, the last one read.

maps.description: How a record becomes an item, by name; each request names one.

HttpBaseUrl.description: Where every request goes: an https URL, or http on this computer (127.0.0.1, localhost) for a local service. No query and no trailing slash; request paths follow it.

HttpHeaderName.description: An HTTP header name other than Authorization, Cookie and Host.

HttpAuth.description: How the core sends the instance's token: the secret setting it reads, in a header with a prefix. Authorization: Bearer <token> when header and prefix are absent.

setting.description: A secret instance setting (secret: true), required: the token.

prefix.description: Bearer and a space when absent; empty sends the token alone.

HttpRequest.description: One GET request and the pages after it.

query.description: Query parameters, encoded by the core.

items.description: Where the records are in the response: a JSON pointer to an array; empty for a response that is the array.

maxPages.description: Pages read at most; 10 when absent.

map.description: The name of the map in maps that makes its records items.

HttpPageNext.description: link: the Link header's rel="next"; body: a URL in the response.

HttpPagination.description: Where the next page is: link, the URL of rel="next" in the Link header (RFC 8288); body, the URL at pointer in the response. A next URL on another origin ends the request. Absent: one page.

JsonPointer.description: A JSON pointer (RFC 6901): empty for the whole value, else /name/0/name.

HttpItemMap.description: How one record becomes an item of kind: each item field (specs/item/v0) from a value of the record. The core sets source; a record whose item does not fit specs/item/v0 is skipped.

fields.description: By item field: id and title always, then updatedAt, status, due, project, deepLink, raw.

HttpValue.description: One item field's value: a JSON pointer into the record (empty is the whole record), or an object that reads one and shapes it. A null or missing value leaves the field out, unless default gives one.

HttpRead.description: Read the value at pointer and shape it.

after.description: Keep the text after the last occurrence of this text; a value without it is missing.

values.description: Replace the value, as text, by the one it names; one it does not name is missing.

default.description: The value when the pointer reads nothing, or nothing that values or after keep.

HttpConst.description: The same value for every record.

ConnectorResource.description: One kind of item the connector brings in, and the commands that act on it.

actions.description: Command ids, each one the plugin declares in contributes.commands: actions are commands.

live.description: The connector can answer queries for this kind directly, beyond what the index holds (a live search).

ConnectorSyncMode.description: pull: the core asks every interval; push: the connector says when something changed; both.

intervalSeconds.description: Between pulls; the core may wait longer (battery, metered networks, rate limits). 900 when absent.

ConnectorSettingName.description: An instance setting's name: folder, calendarId, apiKey.

ConnectorSettingKind.description: The JSON type of an instance setting's value.

ConnectorSetting.description: One instance setting. A secret one is a string the core keeps in the OS keychain and never lists back; it has no default.

default.description: The value until the person sets one. Any JSON value of the kind.

required.description: The instance cannot connect without it.

ConnectorInstance.description: One connection of a connector, as the host lists it. Secret settings are never in settings.

title.description: The name the person gave it: Work calendar.

settings.description: The values of its settings that are not secret.

ConnectorState.description: connected and current; syncing now; stale (the last sync is too old, the items stay readable); error (see error); paused by the person.

ConnectorError.description: Why an instance is in error.

message.description: One sentence to show the person.

reauth.description: Signing in again would fix it.

ConnectorSyncResult.description: What one sync step brought: the changes since the cursor the core passed in.

cursor.description: Where the next step starts; the core keeps it per instance and passes it back. Absent: the next sync starts over.

done.description: false: more changes are waiting, ask again at once with cursor.
